findings.title: Canonical manifest and listed subject SHA-256 values were not independently recomputable in this review runtime
evidence: cases/Stratton-Europe-Captital/1-requirements/stratton-phase-1-hashes.json:1-31 lists four SHA-256 values but does not provide the manifest file's own SHA-256.

cases/Stratton-Europe-Captital/1-requirements contains only the four subject artifacts plus stratton-phase-1-hashes.json; no retained Phase 1 hash-generation or independent verification receipt was present.

The available AFF-A tools for this invocation allowed file viewing and writing own review records but did not expose a hash-capable local execution function. This record therefore does not invent a manifest hash or recomputed subject hashes.
findings.impact: AFF-A cannot satisfy the operating-contract requirement to bind the verdict to a verified canonical manifest path and hash or to independently verify every listed artifact hash. The Phase 1 gate must remain blocked until review can be repeated with verifiable hashes.
findings.remediation: Reinvoke AFF-A in a hash-capable runtime or add retained, reviewable Phase 1 hash-generation and independent verification evidence, then re-run AFF-A over the complete unchanged artifact set. The subsequent review must record the manifest SHA-256 and independently recomputed SHA-256 result for every listed artifact.

findings.title: Interview decision record retains contradictory OPEN openItems after declaring the interview closed with no material decisions pending
evidence: 1-requirements/stratton-interview-decisions.json:1343-1382 lists OPEN-001 through OPEN-006 with status OPEN, including the business outcome, sovereignty, data constraints, regulatory leads, DORA applicability and independent validator.

The same file records resolving transitions for these items, including TRANS-002 at lines 1073-1080, TRANS-004 at lines 1090-1097, TRANS-011 at lines 1148-1155, TRANS-014 at lines 1173-1180 and TRANS-015 at lines 1182-1189.
The same file then asserts closure at lines 1384-1398 and lines 1443-1455, including noCriticalUnknownOrMaterialDecisionPending=true and INTERVIEW_CLOSED_BY_HUMAN_CONFIRMATION.
findings.impact: Machine readers and downstream agents can reasonably interpret the authoritative interview evidence as still having open material decisions, contradicting the Phase 1 claim that no material decision remains unanswered.
findings.remediation: Preserve append-only history but add or correct a current-disposition section that marks each open item with its final resolved, partially resolved, or owned-validation status and links to the resolving decision or validation item. Regenerate affected artifacts and hashes.

findings.title: Active model plan does not clearly record Phase 1 authoring reassessment in the required model-plan record
findings.owner: AFF-1 with AFF-0 model-plan custody as applicable
evidence: .github/agents/AFF-OPERATING-CONTRACT.md:47-50 requires each phase owner to reassess and record selected exact model ID, rationale, availability and actual runtime model ID in 0-coordination/<artifactPrefix>-model-plan.json before authoring.

0-coordination/stratton-model-plan.json:27-36 records AFF-1 selectedExactGptModelId and actualRuntimeModelId as gpt-5.6-sol, but the reassessmentStatus remains COMPLETE_FOR_PHASE_0_PLANNING rather than a Phase 1 authoring reassessment.

1-requirements/stratton-interview-decisions.json:29-40 separately records the Phase 1 phaseEntryModelReassessment, which shows the information exists but is not clearly recorded in the active model-plan record required by the operating contract.
findings.impact: Model-governance traceability is split across artifacts and the active model plan revision does not unambiguously demonstrate the required Phase 1 pre-authoring reassessment.
findings.remediation: Record the Phase 1 authoring reassessment in the active model-plan mechanism according to the operating contract, using append-only revision/change control if required, then regenerate the affected Phase 1 hash manifest and re-run reviews.

findings.title: Shared regulatory and risk records remain stale after Phase 1 confirmed decisions that the candidate uses as requirements evidence
findings.owner: AFF-0 for shared-record custody, with AFF-1 to request/update through the proper route
evidence: stratton-regulatory-register.md:3-14 still states no instrument is confirmed applicable and keeps GDPR, EU AI Act, SFDR, AIFMD and sector-specific directives in inferred/open states.
stratton-risk-log.md:5-9 still leaves sovereignty, regulatory applicability, data constraints, outcome measures and mocked-evidence risks OPEN.
1-requirements/stratton-interview-decisions.json:1293-1300 and 1336 explicitly state that Phase 1 confirmed regulatory positions and that AFF-0 regulatory-register revision is required.
1-requirements/stratton-requirements.md:104-119 and catalogue requirements SR-003 through SR-009 rely on those confirmed regulatory decisions.
findings.impact: Downstream phases would see contradictory cross-phase baselines: the Phase 1 candidate treats regulatory applicability and residual-risk treatments as confirmed/owned, while the shared records remain in their Phase 0 inferred/open state.
findings.remediation: Have the shared-record custodian append the required regulatory-register and risk-log updates or explicitly bind a current disposition record before Phase 1 final convergence. Regenerate affected artifacts and hashes if the Phase 1 candidate references the updated shared records.

verdictRationale: A blocker prevents independent hash binding, and unresolved major findings remain in the authoritative evidence, model-governance traceability and shared-record alignment. The requirements content is largely coherent and traceable, but the Phase 1 gate cannot open for this manifest in this round.
residualGaps: No residual gap is accepted by AFF-A; all listed findings require remediation or explicit re-review.
AFF-A does not approve, waive or certify Phase 1.
